title: Data Handling and Presentation: Tally Marks, Pictographs and Bar Graphs
seo_title: Data Handling and Presentation Class 6 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 4)
standard_code: Class 6, Chapter 4: Data Handling and Presentation
standard_text: Collecting and organising data, tally marks, pictographs with a scale, and drawing and interpreting bar graphs (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 6)
meta_desc: Class 6 Data Handling and Presentation worksheet (Ganita Prakash Chapter 4): tally marks, pictographs and bar graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Read the key: one symbol may stand for many
key_sub: In a bar graph, read the top of each bar against the scale.
body_html:
How it works

Tally marks are grouped in fives so they are easy to count: |||| ||| = 8.

In a pictograph, each picture stands for a number given in the key. If ● = 10, then ●●●◐ = 35.

A bar graph uses bars of equal width; the height of each bar shows the value on the scale.

Example

If ● = 20, what does ●●●● show?

4 × 20

Answer: 80

Example

What number is |||| |||| ||?

5 + 5 + 2

Answer: 12

Common mistakes

  • Counting the symbols in a pictograph without using the key.
  • Ignoring a half symbol.
  • Reading the next grid line instead of the top of the bar.

faq.a: Marks used to count, grouped in fives (four strokes with a fifth across) so the total is quick to read.
A chart that uses pictures; the key tells how many items each picture stands for.
A graph of bars of equal width whose heights show the values against a scale.
